newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudanese rebels say major offensive in northeast.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebels say major offensive in northeast.

text.p: Sudanese rebel leader John Garang said on Friday rebels were mounting a major offensive in the northeast of Africa's largest country and were heading for the main road to Port Sudan, a key link with outside world.
Garang said his forces were advancing towards the town of Tokar and Port Sudan and were active on five fronts simultaneously in northeast, south, east and central Sudan.

Garang, leader of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and head of the military command of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coaliition, said rebels seized garrisons at Karora, Itairba and Shabri near the Red Sea coast on Thursday.
"Our forces are now advancing towards Tokar and the Port Sudan-Khartoum strategic route," he said in a statement, adding the new northeast front extended from Port Sudan to Kassala in the south.

Garang said in the garrison at Karora town rebels killed 220 members of the government's forces and captured 329 assault rifles, 90 G-3 rifles, three 60mm mortars, many machineguns and other arms and ammunition including shells and rockets.
"This work in Red Sea state and in Damazin and the siege of Juba and operations in northern Blue Nile and the Nuba Mountains are working simultaneously," the rebel chief added.
He said the thrust towards Port Sudan -- Khartoum's main commercial link to the Red Sea -- was coordinated with opposition groups behind government lines in northeast Sudan.
Tokar is 100 km (60 miles) from the border with Eritrea and 150 km (90 miles) southeast of Port Sudan. The nearest stretch of the Khartoum-Port Sudan road is 100 km (60 miles) northwest of Tokar.

The Sudanese army said on Thursday Eritrean troops and Sudanese rebels were shelling Sudan army positions on Eritrea's border but the rebels and Eritrea's embassy in Cairo denied denied any Eritrean forces were involved.
In Nairobi, SPLA spokesman Sampson Kwaje said on Friday rebels had repulsed a major army counter-offensive 64 km (40 miles) south of the southern capital of Juba on Wednesday.
"Hundreds of enemy dead bodies litter the area while hundreds more were wounded and taken prisoner," he added.
Garang told Reuters in January that part of rebel strategy was to cut communications between Khartoum and Port Sudan, which is about 670 km (420 miles) northeast of the capital.
Northern rebels of the NDA opposition coalition attacked the army on the Sudanese side of the border with Eritrea in January but that offensive failed to win much territory.
Rebel units farther south, led by the southern-based SPLA, captured the Sudanese towns of Kurmuk and Qeissan on the Ethiopian border in an attack coordinated with the northerners.
Sudan's government said Eritreans and Ethiopians did most of the fighting in both attacks but the two countries, despite very poor relations with Khartoum, said their troops had no role.
The campaign against the Islamist government shifted this month to the far south, where the SPLA captured the major town of Yei and began to advance towards the regional capital Juba.
Khartoum says Ugandan troops are fighting alongside rebels in the south but the Ugandan government denies this and accuses Sudan's government of supporting rebels in northern Uganda.

The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north. It and its allies say they want a popular uprising in Khartoum against the Islamist government.
